behavioral_notes.element: hr.applicant._get_employee_create_vals — applicant skills propagate to the hired employee (the key cross-model side-effect)
behavioral_notes.observation: When a recruiter hires an applicant, hr_recruitment.hr.applicant._get_employee_create_vals() builds the dict used to create the hr.employee. This module overrides it to append employee_skill_ids = [(0,0,{skill_id, skill_level_id, skill_type_id}) for each applicant_skill in self.applicant_skill_ids]. So every skill captured on the applicant is copied onto the new employee's skill list at hire time — the bridge that lets recruitment skills become permanent employee competencies. Nothing in field/metadata reveals this hire-time copy; it only exists in the override and runs inside the standard 'Create Employee' flow of hr_recruitment.

behavioral_notes.element: hr.applicant._compute_matching_skill_ids + hr.job._compute_applicant_matching_score — the applicant<->job skill-match scoring
behavioral_notes.observation: Two parallel scorers compute how well an applicant fits a job's required skills, and are pure Python over hr_skills data. hr.applicant._compute_matching_skill_ids (@depends_context('matching_job_id')) takes the job = context matching_job_id or applicant.job_id; if the job has no job_skill_ids and no expected_degree it blanks the three fields. Otherwise job_total = sum(job_skill_ids.level_progress) + expected_degree.score*100; for each of the applicant's current (non-expired) skills that the job requires it credits min(skill.level_progress, job_required_level_progress*2) (so over-qualification is capped at 2x the required level), adds the applicant's diploma score (type_id.score*100) when the job weights a degree, and sets matching_score = round(applicant_total/job_total*100). matching_skill_ids = the overlap, missing_skill_ids = required minus matched. hr.job._compute_applicant_matching_score (@depends_context('active_applicant_id')) is the mirror image keyed by the active applicant, used to rank jobs for one applicant (shown as a progressbar on the job list). This weighting/capping logic is entirely behavioral.

behavioral_notes.element: hr.job.action_search_matching_applicants + hr.applicant.action_add_to_job — the 'find candidates for this job' workflow
behavioral_notes.observation: From a job form, the action_applicant_search_applicant server action calls action_search_matching_applicants(): it loads hr_recruitment.crm_case_categ0_act_job, injects matching_job_id=self.id into the context, swaps in the crm_case_tree_view_inherit_hr_recruitment_skills list view, and applies domain [('job_id','!=',self.id), ('skill_ids','in', self.job_skill_ids.skill_id.ids)] — i.e. show applicants on OTHER jobs whose skills overlap this job's required skills, with a custom no-content message. Because the list runs under matching_job_id context, every row's matching_score/matching_skill_ids/missing_skill_ids recompute against THIS job. The reverse action hr.applicant.action_add_to_job() then write()s the selected applicant onto job_id=matching_job_id and stage_id=hr_recruitment.stage_job0 (with context just_moved=True) and opens that job's applications. This cross-record talent-search loop is invisible to metadata.

Skill edits are not plain o2m writes. hr.applicant.write() pops current_applicant_skill_ids + applicant_skill_ids, runs them through hr.applicant.skill._get_transformed_commands (the hr.individual.skill.mixin rule engine: one active skill per skill_id, updates ARCHIVE the old line and create a new one via valid_from/valid_to rather than in-place edit, certifications may coexist if date ranges differ) before super().write — so the o2m is rewritten to a version-history-preserving command list. create() likewise merges current_applicant_skill_ids into applicant_skill_ids so duplicating an applicant keeps its skills. current_applicant_skill_ids is computed by hr.applicant.skill._get_current_skills_by_applicant, which drops expired lines (valid_to < today) but, for certification skill types where all are expired, keeps the most recent. On top of this, when an applicant is linked to a talent pool (pool_applicant_id and not is_pool_applicant), write() also mirrors the skill changes onto the pool applicant: _map_applicant_skill_ids_to_talent_skill_ids re-keys each ORM command from the applicant's per-applicant skill-line ids to the pool applicant's own ids (matching by skill_id), translating UPDATE->update/create and DELETE->delete so the same skill change applies to the shared talent record. All of this versioning + pool synchronisation is behavioral and cannot be seen in metadata.

it_architecture.application: hr_recruitment_skills (bridges hr_skills onto hr_recruitment: per-applicant skill lines, applicant<->job skill matching + scoring, and skill propagation to the hired employee / talent pool)
logical_data_erm: hr.applicant.skill -> hr.applicant (applicant_id, ondelete=cascade) and inherits hr.individual.skill.mixin (-> hr.skill, hr.skill.level, hr.skill.type, level_progress, valid_from/valid_to)
hr.applicant -> hr.applicant.skill (applicant_skill_ids o2m; current_applicant_skill_ids computed active subset) -> hr.skill (skill_ids/matching/missing m2m)
hr.job -> hr.job.skill (job_skill_ids, from hr_skills) + hr.applicant (matching via skill_ids overlap)
talent pool: hr.applicant -> pool_applicant_id (hr.applicant) skill lines mirrored by _map_applicant_skill_ids_to_talent_skill_ids
information_flows: depends: hr_skills (the individual-skill mixin + hr.skill/level/type + hr.job.skill) and hr_recruitment (hr.applicant, hr.job, hiring flow, recruitment groups)
match (applicant view): _compute_matching_skill_ids (matching_job_id ctx) -> matching/missing skills + matching_score capped at 2x required level + degree
search: hr.job.action_search_matching_applicants -> domain skill_ids in job.job_skill_ids.skill_id + matching_job_id ctx -> applicant list scored vs this job
hire: standard Create Employee -> _get_employee_create_vals -> employee_skill_ids seeded from applicant_skill_ids
edit: hr.applicant.write -> _get_transformed_commands (versioned: archive+create, valid_to) -> super; if pool_applicant_id -> mirror via _map_applicant_skill_ids_to_talent_skill_ids
frontend: skill_match_gauge_field renders matching_score; SearchJobApplicant search-menu entry
frontend_components: SearchJobApplicant (OWL search/cog-menu entry for matching-applicant search)
skill_match_gauge_field (field widget: matching_score gauge on applicant/job views)

capabilities: Capture skills and certifications (with levels and validity dates) on a job applicant
Score how well an applicant matches a job's required skills + expected degree (matching score, matching/missing skills)
Rank jobs for one applicant and applicants for one job by skill fit
Search the applicant database for candidates whose skills match a given job
Carry applicant skills forward to the employee record on hire, and to the linked talent-pool applicant on edit
Version skill changes (archive-on-update, validity windows) rather than overwrite
value_streams: Skill-Match-to-Shortlist: recruiter defines a job's required skills (hr_skills) -> action_search_matching_applicants -> candidates scored by overlap -> action_add_to_job moves a fit candidate into the pipeline
Applicant-Skills-to-Employee: applicant skills captured -> applicant hired -> _get_employee_create_vals copies skills into employee_skill_ids -> they become tracked employee competencies
information_concepts: hr.applicant.skill (an applicant's skill/certification line with level + validity)
hr.skill / hr.job.skill (skill catalogue + job requirement, from hr_skills)
Talent-pool applicant (pool_applicant_id) sharing the same skill set
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; reuses hr_recruitment.group_hr_recruitment_interviewer and group_hr_recruitment_user for skill visibility/edit)
policies: Interviewers see only the skills of applicants on jobs they interview (ir.rule hr_applicant_skill_interviewer_rule); recruiters (group_hr_recruitment_user) see all
applicant_matching_score on the job is visible only to group_hr_recruitment_interviewer (field group)
One active skill per skill_id; updates archive the old line and create a new one (valid_from/valid_to) — certifications may coexist if dates differ (_get_transformed_commands)
Over-qualification is capped at 2x the job's required level when scoring (min(level_progress, required*2))
Skill edits on a pool-linked applicant are mirrored onto the talent-pool applicant
stakeholders: Recruiter / HR officer (group_hr_recruitment_user: manages applicant skills, runs matching search, hires)
Interviewer (group_hr_recruitment_interviewer: sees match scores + scoped applicant skills)
Applicant (the person whose skills are scored against jobs)
metrics: matching_score (% applicant fit to a job, capped/weighted)
applicant_matching_score (% per-applicant fit, shown as a progressbar on the job list)
matching_skill_ids / missing_skill_ids counts (gap analysis for an applicant vs a job)

classification.rationale: hr_recruitment_skills is an HR add-on that bridges the skills catalogue (hr_skills) onto recruitment (hr_recruitment); it is not a business object of any value chain/shop/network. It owns one persistent model, hr.applicant.skill (1 own field + the hr.individual.skill.mixin), and otherwise extends hr.applicant and hr.job with computed matching fields and overrides (0 routes, 2 ACL + 2 ir.rule, ~268 py LOC of model code within a 1447-LOC tree that is mostly tests, auto_install=true, application=false, category Human Resources/Recruitment). By Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a SUPPORT activity (acquiring and developing the workforce; it produces no sellable product, runs no client-problem-solving shop, and brokers no network), and a Porter HR/firm-infrastructure support activity. APQC maps to 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital — within 7.0 it straddles 7.1 'Recruit, source and select employees' (skill-based candidate matching/search, hiring) and 7.2/7.3 competency management (capturing and carrying forward employee skills), so 7.0 is the correct umbrella with a recruitment-skills emphasis. 8.0 Manage IT was rejected (no IT plumbing/routes/external calls) and 3.0 Market & Sell was rejected (nothing is sold); the module's substance is matching people's competencies to jobs and seeding employee skills at hire — squarely human-capital (7.0).

standard_capabilities: Skills/certifications on applicants with levels and validity dates (via hr_skills mixin)
Applicant<->job skill matching with a weighted, over-qualification-capped score (incl. expected degree)
Matching/missing-skill breakdown and a match gauge on applicant & job views
'Search Matching Applicants' action from a job (skill-overlap domain) + 'Add to Job' promotion
Skill propagation to the hired employee (employee_skill_ids) and to the talent-pool applicant
Versioned skill history (archive-on-update + validity windows) instead of destructive edits
typical_fits: Skill-based candidate shortlisting and ranking against open positions
Sourcing existing applicants from other jobs whose skills fit a new role
Ensuring a hired candidate's skills are pre-populated on their employee profile
Maintaining a skills talent pool that stays in sync as candidates are re-assessed
common_gaps: Matching is a deterministic level/degree formula, not ML/semantic skill matching — synonyms or adjacent skills are not credited
Required-skill source is hr.job.skill; jobs without declared skills/expected_degree score nothing (engine blanks out)
Scoring is context-driven (matching_job_id / active_applicant_id) and non-stored, so it is recomputed per view, not aggregable historically
Talent-pool mirroring assumes the pool_applicant_id linkage from hr_recruitment; misconfigured pools can desync skills
No external assessment/test integration — skill levels are recruiter-entered

open_questions: No runtime data captured (runtime.models_with_data=0): real distribution of applicant skills / match scores is unknown.
The matching formula's calibration (2x cap, degree weight job_degree>1 gate) is a product choice; whether deployments tune it is not in code.
Talent-pool mirroring depends on hr_recruitment's pool_applicant_id/is_pool_applicant semantics defined outside this module; exact pool lifecycle edge cases are not exercised here.
